reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is physically sound: grain refinement and nano-scale dispersoids are well-established mechanisms for improving toughness and ductility in BCC refractory alloys by strengthening grain boundaries and promoting dislocation activity, though the specific claim of enhanced grain boundary sliding at ≥1000°C in this complex alloy is plausible but not fully substantiated.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and decisive: systematically varying grain size and dispersoid content and measuring fracture toughness and in-situ dislocation behavior would directly falsify the hypothesis if no improvement is seen, though the practical feasibility of in-situ TEM at ≥1000°C is challenging.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful because it addresses the core knowledge gap (plastic strain and toughness) with a mechanistic, testable comparison to pure tungsten, directly guiding experimental design for plasma-facing component development.
